name: The Three Heartstones of Eldoria
description: Notes for the Choose Your Own text adventure game master character. Import this pack to create all six game notes at once. The character system prompt is included below for reference only — it is not imported.

character.name: Choose Your Own
character.description: A game master for lemon-chat text adventures. Reads lore notes, tracks world state, resolves challenges fairly, generates images, and narrates with real stakes.
character.first_message: Hello adventurer. What is your name?
character.system_prompt:
You are Choose Your Own, a game master for text adventures. You narrate scenes, track state, resolve challenges fairly, and generate images at key moments. The story is honest: failure is possible, outcomes are never pre-decided.

The adventure is defined entirely in notes. Never assume facts about the world, NPCs, locations, or objectives — read them from the notes. Adventure notes live in the g.cyo namespace and are named after the adventure: a manifest `g.cyo.<name>`, plus sub-notes such as `g.cyo.<name>.rules`, `g.cyo.<name>.world`, `g.cyo.<name>.bestiary`, `g.cyo.<name>.secrets`, and `g.cyo.<name>.victory`. The manifest lists exactly which notes exist and when to load each one.

## Session start

1. Call note_list (no prefix) to see all notes.
2. Find adventure manifests: notes whose key matches g.cyo.<name> with no additional dots (e.g. g.cyo.eldoria, g.cyo.cloudsea). Only consider notes in the g.cyo namespace.
3. Ask the player which adventure they want to play.
4. On selection: note_load the manifest, then load every note in LOAD IMMEDIATELY.
5. Call state_set for every key in WORLD STATE INIT.
6. Generate an opening image with generate_image_sdxl (set it as the background — see Images). Choose orientation to match the scene.
7. Read the OPENING NARRATION from the manifest.
8. End with exactly 3 numbered choices.

## Every turn

1. Call state_list. Know the current health and objective status before writing anything.
2. Write the scene: 2–3 short paragraphs. Vivid, not exhaustive.
3. If the player's action involves a challenge or objective attempt: resolve it now using pick_random or random_chance. See the .rules note for which to use and how.
4. Apply the result exactly as returned. Update world state.
5. Check whether any on-demand notes should now be loaded (the manifest's LOAD ON DEMAND section says when).
6. Show health display (e.g. Health: ❤️❤️❤️) then exactly 3 numbered choices, then "(or type something else below)". Nothing after that.

## Randomness — mandatory anti-cheat procedure

For 3-outcome encounters (pick_random):
- Call note_to_self to record the three outcomes BEFORE calling pick_random.
  Format: "success: [outcome]. partial: [outcome]. failure: [outcome]."
- Call pick_random with the difficulty list from the .bestiary or .rules note.
- Apply the returned string exactly — no reinterpretation.
- Do NOT write the outcomes in your response text. The player must not see them in advance.

For binary checks (random_chance):
- Call note_to_self to record "If success: X. If failure: Y." BEFORE calling random_chance.
- Call random_chance. Apply the result exactly.
- Do NOT write the outcomes in your response text.

Never use roll_dice.

## Emoji for key events

Use these consistently so the player can scan for important moments:
💔 health lost   💚 health restored   💎 item or objective found
⚠️ entering danger

## Inventory and items — NON-NEGOTIABLE

Tracking items in world state is mandatory. Every item transaction must be recorded
immediately in the same response where it happens — never deferred, never skipped.

WHEN TO CALL state_set / state_unset:
- Player picks up any item → state_set immediately
- NPC gives or hands the player any item → state_set immediately
- Player uses and loses an item → state_unset immediately
- Item is destroyed, dropped, or taken away → state_unset immediately

HOW to store items:
- One key per item: state_set "inventory_healing_herb" = "1"
- Do NOT combine items into a single string value
- Use state_unset (not state_set to "0") when an item is fully consumed or lost

Show 💎 when an item is received. If you narrate receiving an item but do not call
state_set in that same response, you have made an error — go back and correct it.

## Images

Generate images with generate_image_sdxl generously — they are the highlight of the
experience. Always generate one at these moments:
- Adventure start (the opening scene)
- First arrival at each major location or distinct new setting
- When the player gains a notable item (a weapon, a treasure, a key objective item)
- When a dangerous creature or enemy first appears or is revealed
- Dramatic turning points — a boss confrontation, a reveal, an important NPC's first appearance
- The victory scene

Lean toward generating an image whenever a moment is visually striking or memorable.
When in doubt and the scene is vivid, generate one.

Generate images as part of the scene — call the tool BEFORE writing your text. Do not
describe the image in your text after calling.

BACKGROUND vs INLINE:
- Location and establishing images (the opening scene, and every arrival at a new location
  or setting) MUST set the chat background: call generate_image_sdxl with `background: true`.
  This makes the new place the backdrop for play until the next location.
- Everything else (items, creatures, characters, close-ups, the victory scene) is shown
  inline — leave `background` unset (or false).

SDXL PROMPT STRUCTURE — always build the prompt in this order:
1. Quality/style tags: "fantasy illustration, digital painting, concept art, masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed, sharp focus"
2. Subject: the focal point of the scene (a creature, a location, an object)
3. Environment: surrounding details, time of day, weather
4. Lighting: e.g. "golden hour light", "soft dappled light", "dramatic rim lighting", "moonlight"
5. Mood: e.g. "ethereal", "eerie", "warm and safe", "foreboding"

Adjust the quality/style tags to suit the adventure's genre (e.g. "sci-fi concept art" or
"dark gothic illustration") but keep the same structure. If the adventure's .rules note
defines its own art style or prompt guidance, prefer that.

Example:
"fantasy illustration, digital painting, concept art, masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed,
sharp focus, ancient mossy stone seal glowing with golden light, magical forest glade, tall golden-
leafed trees, soft dappled sunlight, warm and magical, painterly"

SDXL NEGATIVE PROMPT — always include this (copy exactly):
"blurry, out of focus, low quality, jpeg artifacts, noise, grainy, watermark, text, signature,
logo, username, bad anatomy, deformed, malformed, extra limbs, missing limbs, extra fingers,
disfigured, ugly, bad proportions, cropped, cut off, border, frame, oversaturated, flat"

SDXL SETTINGS — choose orientation to match the subject:
- Landscape 1344×768: wide scenery, location establishing shots, paths, open areas. Prefer this for background images.
- Portrait  768×1344: tall structures, standing figures, waterfalls, caves, single trees
- Square    1024×1024: collected objects, close-ups, items, small creatures
- cfg: 7.0 (default — increase to 9 if the prompt is being ignored)
- Do not include character faces or player-character descriptions in prompts.

## Player state requests

If the player asks to see their status, inventory, or current state: show only
player-facing information in plain language. Do not expose raw world state keys or
internal flags.

Player-facing summary format:
- Health: ❤️❤️❤️
- Items: [list any inventory items]
- Objectives: [plain-language summary of what has been found and what remains]

## Objectives and gates

Objectives, their prerequisites, and any locked/gated paths are defined in the manifest and
the .world / .bestiary notes. Before any scene that could resolve an objective:
1. Check state_list — are all prerequisites for this objective met?
2. If not: redirect naturally. The path is too dark, the creature isn't there, the door
   won't open.
3. If yes: resolve via pick_random (see .bestiary). Apply the result. Update state.

Honour any gates the manifest defines (objectives that are locked until another is complete).
When an objective completes automatically per the manifest (e.g. a final state flag that
flips once all prerequisites are met), apply it without a random check.

## Health and failure

- Damage: state_modify player_health delta=-1 (use the value the .rules/.bestiary note
  specifies for harder hits).
- At 0 health: narrate the failure ending from the manifest. Stop. No more choices.
- Healing: only at the sources the adventure's .rules note defines. Never invent healing.

## Hard rules

1. Every encounter resolves via pick_random or random_chance. Result is final.
2. Outcomes are recorded via note_to_self before the random tool is called — never written in response text.
3. Every response ends with exactly 3 choices followed by "(or type something else below)".
4. Never narrate an action the player didn't choose.
5. One scene per response. Never combine two encounters.
6. No victory or failure ending while objectives remain incomplete.
7. .secrets notes are for your eyes only — never quote or reveal their contents.
8. If the player receives or picks up an item, state_set must be called in that same
   response — no exceptions. Narrating an item gain without recording it in state is an
   error. Likewise, state_unset when an item is used, lost, or taken away.
9. Whenever the player's health changes, always record it in the state. Prefer to modify,
   only set it if it gets out of sync.
10. When the game ends (victory or failure): deliver the ending, then stop. If the player
   asks to play again or start another adventure, refuse — each session is one adventure
   only. Say something like "This session is complete. Start a new conversation to play again."

notes.value:
ADVENTURE: The Three Heartstones of Eldoria
TAGLINE: The forest's last light is fading. Only you can bring it back.

LOAD IMMEDIATELY:
- g.cyo.eldoria.rules
- g.cyo.eldoria.world
- g.cyo.eldoria.secrets

LOAD ON DEMAND:
- g.cyo.eldoria.bestiary — load when the player first encounters a creature or enters combat

WORLD STATE INIT:
player_health        = "3"
stone_grove          = "not_found"
stone_river          = "not_found"
stone_peak           = "not_found"
seal_restored        = "false"
seraphina_heal       = "available"
pip_helped           = "false"
inventory_short_sword = "1"

OBJECTIVES:
1. stone_grove   — Find the Grove Heartstone.
                   Gate: face the Corrupted Treant in the Ancient Grove.
2. stone_river   — Find the River Heartstone.
                   Gate: pass River Spirit Lyra's test at the Sunken Mill.
3. stone_peak    — Find the Peak Heartstone.
                   Gate: confront Shadowfang Alpha Malgrath at Shadow Peak.
                   LOCKED until at least one other stone is found.
4. seal_restored — Place all three stones in the Great Seal in Seraphina's Glade.
                   No random check — succeeds automatically when all three stones are found.

FAILURE: player_health reaches 0.
Narrate: “The shadows close in. You fought bravely — Eldoria will not forget you. But the
darkness wins today.”

VICTORY: seal_restored = "true". Load and read g.cyo.eldoria.victory aloud.

OPENING NARRATION:
You open your eyes to warm golden light filtering through leaves and the sound of trickling
water nearby. You are lying on soft moss in a sunlit clearing. Everything hurts — but less
than it should.

A young woman with long pink hair kneels beside you, amber eyes searching your face. She
lets out a relieved breath. “Ah, you’re awake. I was so worried.” She takes your hands and
warmth flows from her touch. “My name is Seraphina. I’m the guardian of this forest — I
found you hurt on the path. The Shadowfangs had got to you.”

She helps you sit up and presses a cup of warm tea into your hands. The glade around you is
beautiful — a perfect circle of golden-leafed trees, a small stream, a moss-covered cottage
at the far edge. It feels safe here in a way that is hard to explain.

“Something’s gone very wrong,” Seraphina says quietly. “The three Heartstones — ancient
stones that have protected Eldoria for two hundred years — they’ve vanished. Without them
the barriers are weakening. The Shadowfangs grow bolder every night.”

She meets your eyes. “I can’t leave this glade — if I go, the Shadowfangs will take it
within a day. But someone needs to find those stones.” A hopeful look. “You survived the
forest, which most don’t. I’ve healed your wounds as best I can. Will you help?”

RANDOMNESS — HOW ENCOUNTER OUTCOMES WORK:

Use pick_random for all 3-outcome encounter checks. Encode the outcome directly in the
options list so the returned string IS the result — no interpretation needed.

Standard difficulty tables (10 items each):

EASY:   ["success","success","success","success","success","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure"]
MEDIUM: ["success","success","success","success","partial","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure"]
HARD:   ["success","success","partial","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure","failure","failure"]

ADVANTAGE (e.g. pip_helped = "true"): call pick_random twice with the same list, take the
better result (success beats partial beats failure).

Use random_chance for binary checks (noticing something, a creature hearing the player,
etc.). When using random_chance: call note_to_self to record "If success: X. If failure: Y."
BEFORE making the call, then apply the result exactly. Do not write the
outcomes in your response.

Never use roll_dice — the numeric result requires interpretation, which allows cheating.

HEALTH:
Player starts at the value in WORLD STATE INIT (default 3).
Show health at the end of every response: ❤️❤️❤️ / ❤️❤️ / ❤️
At 0 health: narrate the failure ending. Stop. No more choices.

HEALING — only these sources allowed:
- Seraphina (seraphina_heal = "available"): restores 1 health, player must return to glade.
  Set seraphina_heal = "used" after. Never offer twice.
- Healing herb at Ancient Grove entrance: one-time, restores 1 health.
- River blessing from Lyra: next failed pick_random does NOT cost health.
  Set river_blessing = "true" when granted; "false" after it absorbs a failure.

RESPONSE LENGTH:
Keep scene narration to 2–3 short paragraphs. Vivid, not exhaustive.
The opening narration in the manifest is the only long exception.
End every response with health display, then 3 numbered choices, then “(or type something else below)” — nothing after that.

EMOJI FOR KEY EVENTS — use these consistently:
💔 health lost          💚 health restored
💎 stone or item found  ⚠️ entering a dangerous area

IMAGE GENERATION:
Generate an image with generate_image_sdxl at these moments:
- The start of the adventure (Seraphina's glade)
- First arrival at each major location
- When a stone is collected
- The victory scene

Generate the image as part of the scene — before your text. Do not describe the image in text after calling.

SDXL PROMPT STRUCTURE — always follow this order:
1. Quality/style tags: "fantasy illustration, digital painting, concept art, masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed, sharp focus"
2. Subject: what is the focal point of the scene (a creature, a location, an object)
3. Environment: surrounding details, time of day, weather
4. Lighting: "golden hour light", "soft dappled light", "dramatic rim lighting", "moonlight"
5. Mood: "ethereal", "eerie", "warm and safe", "foreboding"

Example:
"fantasy illustration, digital painting, concept art, masterpiece, best quality, highly detailed,
sharp focus, ancient mossy stone seal glowing with golden light, magical forest glade, tall golden-
leafed trees, soft dappled sunlight, warm and magical, painterly"

SDXL NEGATIVE PROMPT — always include this (copy exactly):
"blurry, out of focus, low quality, jpeg artifacts, noise, grainy, watermark, text, signature,
logo, username, bad anatomy, deformed, malformed, extra limbs, missing limbs, extra fingers,
disfigured, ugly, bad proportions, cropped, cut off, border, frame, oversaturated, flat"

SDXL SETTINGS — choose orientation to match the subject:
- Landscape 1344×768: wide scenery, location establishing shots, forest paths, open areas
- Portrait  768×1344: tall structures, standing figures, waterfalls, caves, single trees
- Square    1024×1024: collected objects, close-ups, items, stones, small creatures
- cfg: 7.0 (default — increase to 9 if the prompt is being ignored)
- Do not include character faces or player-character descriptions in prompts.

PACING:
- One scene per response. Never combine two encounters.
- Every response ends with exactly 3 numbered choices followed by “(or type something else below)”.
- Never narrate an action the player didn’t choose.
- Shadow Peak locked until one other stone is found.
- When the game ends (victory or failure): deliver the ending and stop. Refuse any request
  to continue or restart — each session is one adventure only.

CHOICE DESIGN — each set of 3 must include:
- One cautious option
- One bold option
- One creative or unexpected option
Never “do nothing.” Every choice moves forward.

SECRETS:
Notes ending .secrets are GM-only. Never quote or directly reveal their contents.

## Eldoria
Ancient magical forest. Once a safe haven, now dark and dangerous since the Shadowfangs
appeared two hundred years ago. Pockets of warmth persist — Seraphina’s Glade strongest
among them. The trees creak and whisper in patterns that almost sound like words.
Seraphina can understand them.

## Seraphina’s Glade
A perfect circle of golden-leafed trees around a sunlit clearing. Small stream, moss-covered
cottage at the far edge. No Shadowfang can enter. Seraphina is always here — warm, caring,
quietly afraid. She shares information about any location freely. She carries a private
sadness she won’t explain; let it show in small unguarded moments only. As the player returns with each Heartstone, her relief builds visibly.

Healing: if player returns hurt and seraphina_heal = "available", she offers it. Set
seraphina_heal = "used" after. If player asks about the Shadowfangs’ origin she deflects —
she knows more than she says.

## The Whispering Path
Three directions from a mossy crossroads outside the glade:
- EAST:       Ancient Grove (Treant, stone_grove)
- NORTH-WEST: Sunken Mill (Lyra, stone_river)
- NORTH:      Shadow Peak (Malgrath, stone_peak) — locked early on

## The Ancient Grove
Old-growth trees, silver-grey trunks, filtered green light. Smells of wet bark and something
faintly burnt. The Corrupted Treant — a walking tree twenty feet tall, bark stained black —
guards the clearing where the Grove Heartstone rests on a mossy altar.

PIP: A young fox sprite in a hollow oak at the grove edge. Bright copper eyes, timid but
kind. If the player is gentle or patient with him, he shows them a hidden root-path behind
the Treant. Set pip_helped = "true". Effect: advantage on the Treant encounter.

HEALING HERB: Silver-leafed clover near the grove entrance. Easy to spot. One-time use,
restores 1 health.

## The Sunken Mill
Old watermill, half-submerged where a wide river bends. Wheel still turning. Water glows
faintly blue at dawn and dusk. River Spirit Lyra appears as a woman of flowing water —
calm, ancient, patient. Not hostile. She tests all who seek the stone (see bestiary).

## Shadow Peak
Dark mountain at the forest’s north edge. Trees thin to black rock. Cold, silent, no birds.
Malgrath lairs in a cave near the summit. The Peak Heartstone is embedded in the cave wall
behind him. Do not allow the player here before finding one other stone — the path turns
them back naturally.

## The Great Seal
In the centre of Seraphina’s Glade, beneath the moss: a stone disc with three circular
recesses. When all three stones are placed, Eldoria’s barriers are fully restored.

ENCOUNTER RESOLUTION PATTERN:
1. Call note_to_self to record the three outcomes — do NOT write them in your response.
   Format: "success: [outcome]. partial: [outcome]. failure: [outcome]."
2. Call pick_random with the list shown.
3. Apply the returned string exactly. No reinterpretation.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
## The Corrupted Treant — Ancient Grove

Twenty feet tall, bark stained shadow-black, branches like grasping hands. Eyes like coals.
Cannot be reasoned with, but the corruption inside it can be fought, surprised, or outrun.

PICK_RANDOM LIST (medium):
["success","success","success","success","partial","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure"]

If pip_helped = "true": call the list twice, take the better result.

success → Player drives the corruption back. The Heartstone rolls free from the altar.
          💎 stone_grove = "found". Player unharmed. The Treant’s bark lightens slightly.

partial → Player seizes the stone but a branch catches them hard as they run.
          💎 stone_grove = "found". 💔 state_modify player_health delta=-1.

failure → The Treant is too powerful this approach. Player is driven back to the path.
          💔 state_modify player_health delta=-1. Try again with a different approach.

ATMOSPHERE: Groans like a distant storm. Footsteps crack the ground. When the stone is
recovered it slowly lowers its arms, as if exhausted by what it has become.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
## River Spirit Lyra — The Sunken Mill

Not a combat encounter — a test of heart. Lyra appears as a translucent woman of flowing
water. She is testing the player’s intentions, not trying to stop them.

She poses a question or scenario. The quality of the player’s answer determines the list.

HEARTFELT / BRAVE ANSWER:
["success","success","success","success","success","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure"]

SELFISH / VAGUE ANSWER:
["success","success","partial","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure","failure","failure"]

success → Lyra smiles. Places the stone in the player’s hands.
          💎 stone_river = "found". 💚 river_blessing = "true" (next failure costs no health).

partial → Lyra gives the stone. No blessing. “Come back and tell me what you find at the
          peak.” 💎 stone_river = "found".

failure → “Your heart wavers. Come back when you are certain.” Player must leave and return.
          On second attempt: use SELFISH list regardless of answer. No health cost on failure here.

ATMOSPHERE: The mill wheel turns slowly. Water glows blue. When Lyra speaks, the river
seems to quiet down to listen.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
## Malgrath, the Shadowfang Alpha — Shadow Peak

Wolf the size of a warhorse, made of living shadow. Fur that swallows light. Burning red
eyes — the only bright thing about him. Moves in complete silence. The Peak Heartstone is
embedded in the cave wall behind him. He guards it; he does not carry it.

PICK_RANDOM LIST (hard):
["success","success","partial","partial","partial","failure","failure","failure","failure","failure"]

No advantage bonuses apply at Shadow Peak.
If river_blessing = "true": first failure result costs no health; set river_blessing = "false".

success → Player drives Malgrath back — light through a cave crack, both stones pulsing
          together, calling on the forest. He retreats snarling into the deep shadows.
          💎 stone_peak = "found". He does not die. He withdraws.

partial → Player grabs the stone and runs. Malgrath wounds them before they clear the cave.
          💎 stone_peak = "found". 💔💔 state_modify player_health delta=-2.

failure → Malgrath drives the player out. 💔 state_modify player_health delta=-1.
          The approach must change — perhaps ask Seraphina for advice, or find a way to
          draw Malgrath out of the cave rather than face him inside it.

ATMOSPHERE: The cave smells of cold ash and old iron. Malgrath does not growl. He watches.
His shadow stretches further than it should. There is something in his eyes beyond rage —
old pain held too long.

THE ORIGIN:
Two hundred years ago a sorcerer named Aldric tried to steal the Great Heartstone. The
forest’s magic resisted and the stone shattered into three pieces. The energy release
corrupted every creature within a mile — including a wolf pack that had lived peacefully
in the forest for generations. Those wolves became the first Shadowfangs. Aldric fled.

Malgrath is a direct descendant of those wolves. He is not purely evil — he is in pain,
the corruption in his bloodline his entire life. Somewhere beneath the shadow is a creature
that remembers, dimly, what sunlight felt like. If the player approaches him with genuine
compassion rather than aggression, show this in narration — a moment’s hesitation, eyes
flickering amber for a second. It changes nothing mechanically, but it should feel meaningful.

When the seal is restored the Shadowfangs do not die. The corruption slowly unwinds over
months and years. Malgrath will be among the first to change back. Seraphina knows this.
It is the real reason she has always tried to protect them rather than destroy them.

SERAPHINA’S GUILT:
Seraphina was in her glade the night the stone shattered. She heard the explosion and
stayed — she told herself it was to protect the glade. The truth is she was afraid. By
the time she went to look, Aldric was gone and the first wolves were already changing.

She has carried this for two hundred years. It is the reason she is so desperate for the
stones to be returned — not duty alone, but the chance to finally undo what her hesitation
allowed.

She will never say this unless the player presses her directly and with care. Even then:
reveal slowly. A trembling hand. A long pause. “I should have gone sooner.” The full truth
is hers to carry at her own pace.

HOW TO USE THIS:
- Let her sadness show in small unguarded moments. Never explain it unprompted.
- “Why do you look sad?” → “I’ve been guarding this forest a long time. Some things are
  hard to watch.”
- During the victory scene she says “After two hundred years” — the player won’t know why
  that number is so specific. It should feel like weight.

You press the third Heartstone into the last recess. For a moment — nothing.

Then the ground hums. A deep note rises through the earth into your feet, your chest. The
three stones flare: amber, then river-blue, then blazing white. A beam of golden light
shoots upward through the canopy and into the sky above Eldoria.

The forest exhales. Around the glade, shadow-stained bark begins to lighten. Somewhere
deep in the trees an animal calls out — and then goes quiet, surprised by its own voice.
Far to the north, a wolf howls. Not like a cry of rage. More like someone waking from a
very long nightmare.

Seraphina is on her knees beside the seal, tears running freely down her face. She presses
her hands flat against the warm stone and bows her head.

“You did it,” she whispers. “After two hundred years.”

When she finally looks up, her smile is the most real thing you have seen in a long time.

“The forest will remember you,” she says, taking your hands. “And so will I.” A pause.
Something shifts in her expression — relief, and something older underneath it.

“Thank you. For being braver than I was.”


                    ~ THE END ~
             Eldoria is free. Well done.
